resolved.title: The Vacuus of the Queens
resolved.abstract: Which faces of a reflection polytope lie on the mirrors of its group can be read from its Coxeter chain. Theorem 1 (the Mirror Law): for the Wythoff polytope of a seed x and a node set J of size n-2 giving its (n-2)-faces, the faces of type J lie on mirrors exactly when the roots of the unringed nodes include one orthogonal to every simple root in J; checked against direct measurement in 228 cases across A3, B3, H3, A4, B4, F4 and H4. Corollary 2: every face of a regular polytope lies on a mirror; the 1200 triangles of the 600-cell and the 720 pentagons of the 120-cell (DICTO's White and Red Queens) lie on the same 60 central slices, the mirrors of H4, 20 triangles and 12 pentagons on each. Corollary 3: for a four-node chain and the seed (0,1,1,0) the faces of the end bonds lie on mirrors and the faces of the middle bond on none; in B4 and H4 these are exactly the faces between cells of different kinds. Corollary 4 places the edges of DICTONIC's golden loop T(x) on or off the three coordinate mirrors. The central slices carrying a polytope's faces are its Vacuus, DICTO's construction.
